label: original-phase input g/u/3/b/p shortly after m/z/o/w/x/t/0
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (95% of mass), mostly at t=2-5, never at t=0, and mostly on the first occurrence of a token. The current input token is the main driver: g (34% of mass, 9x lift), then u, 3, b, p. Activation is much higher when one of m/z/o/w/x/t/0 came one or two steps earlier (the top examples look like m o o g or w x z g). It also fires weakly at the first copy step that outputs orig(1) (recall_idx 1, about 5% of mass). It is nearly silent during the delimiter step and the rest of the copy phase. Magnitude is largest for g after m/z/o/w context. The token-set predicate gets only about 0.2 precision: many steps with g/u/3/b/p after those letters stay inactive, so the unit seems to read a mixed hidden-state direction that this predicate only roughly matches. Dev F1 0.31, mass recall 0.67.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: g, u; t=2: g, u, 3, b; t=3: g, u, 3, b) and the first original token (most: m, w, a, k, n, x; least: u, p, i, g); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=9, L=6 & t=7.
